01-10-men.name: 10 Men
01-10-men.description: 10 Men is a large format menswear magazine from London, published twice a year to follow the men's collections. Each issue is organised around a trio of themed words and runs long fashion stories, cover interviews with actors and musicians, and conversations with designers, with several collectable covers per issue. It suits readers who follow luxury menswear and fashion photography closely.
01-10-men.note: Legal entity not shown on the publisher site; recorded under the imprint name 10 Magazine. Issue 64 has several covers; the Hermes cover is used.

02-10-women.name: 10 Magazine
02-10-women.description: 10 Magazine is the womenswear title from the same London house as 10 Men, appearing twice a year in step with the collections. Issues carry long photographic stories built around individual luxury houses, interviews with designers, models and musicians, and a dozen or so alternative covers. It is for readers who want high fashion imagery in a thick, seasonal object.
02-10-women.note: CSV said 10 Women; the publisher calls the women's edition 10 Magazine. No cover of Issue 77 above 584px was found anywhere.

03-a-dance-mag.name: a Dance Mag
03-a-dance-mag.description: a Dance Mag is a small format English language magazine about dance as it is lived around the world, from ritual and folk forms to club floors and contemporary stages. Each issue takes one theme and fills it with essays, reportage, interviews and a photographic poster insert. It is for dancers, scholars and anyone curious about movement as culture rather than as performance review.
03-a-dance-mag.note: London is the registered address; the editorial team is spread across several cities. Cadence has been irregular (issues in 2018, 2019, 2020, then two in 2025). No publisher shop, so no publisher cover price.

04-a-magazine-curated-by.name: A Magazine Curated By
04-a-magazine-curated-by.description: Each issue of this Paris fashion title is handed to a single designer or house, who fills it with their own references, from photography and art to music, places and friends. The result reads as a portrait of a designer's mind rather than a season's coverage, and recent guests include Cecilie Bahnsen and Hiroshi Fujiwara. It is for readers interested in how designers think and for collectors of fashion publications.
04-a-magazine-curated-by.note: Publisher legal name is A Publisher SAS. N°30 was still marked pre-order on the publisher site while already launched and listed by KD Presse; recorded as October 2026.

05-acid-magazine.name: Acid Magazine
05-acid-magazine.description: Acid Magazine is a thick bilingual French and English annual that uses surfing as a way into the ocean itself, taking in oceanography, coastal economies, environmental questions, art, fashion and history. The latest number runs to 400 pages and fifteen stories in a compact format, issued with four different covers. It suits readers of surf and ocean culture who want essays and photography rather than contest results or gear.
05-acid-magazine.note: City (Douarnenez) comes from a stockist listing; the publisher site only says printed in Brittany. No8 has four random covers; one design is used.

06-adbusters.name: Adbusters
06-adbusters.description: Adbusters is the Vancouver bimonthly that has been attacking consumer culture since 1989, mixing political and philosophical essays with spoof advertisements, collage and hand lettered design in an almost ad free package. Recent issues take on AI driven culture and the state of liberal politics. It is read by activists, designers and students interested in media criticism and culture jamming.
06-adbusters.note: Issue date from the subscription mailing schedule (#187 late September 2026). Price USD 12.50 from the publisher shop. No flat cover image found; both candidates are product shots. The CSV hint of June 2026 does not match the publisher's schedule.

07-alei-journal.name: Aleï Journal
07-alei-journal.description: Aleï Journal is a Paris photography and art publication that gives long portfolio runs to image makers with raw or unconventional practices and keeps text to a minimum. Each issue appears with several alternative covers by different photographers. It is for readers of contemporary fashion and art photography and for collectors of photo publications.
07-alei-journal.note: Publisher site is a minimal portfolio with no imprint or shop; Paris rests on distributor descriptions. Stockists call it biannual but the cadence since 2024 is about one issue a year, so frequency is annual. Price EUR 30 is from KD Presse, the publisher's designated sales channel.

09-antidote.name: Antidote Magazine
09-antidote.description: Antidote Magazine is a French fashion and culture title built on long interviews and black and white portrait series with musicians, writers and actors, many from the French rap and pop scene. Since 2026 each issue comes as a large 30 by 40 cm revue and a cheaper pocket fanzine with the same contents, each with several covers. It is for French speaking readers who follow music, fashion and youth culture and want a collectable object.
09-antidote.note: Legal entity Antidote SAS, Paris. N°30 (Autumn Winter 2026) was on pre-order on 17 November 2026, so N°29 is recorded as the latest issue out. Price is the revue format.

10-applied-arts.name: Applied Arts
10-applied-arts.description: Applied Arts is a Canadian magazine for the visual communications trade, covering advertising, graphic design, photography and illustration. Its two issues a year are largely awards annuals presenting the winners of the magazine's own competitions alongside interviews and features on creative practice. It is bought by designers, art directors, photographers and marketing people, mainly in Canada.
10-applied-arts.note: Trade and awards title; please decide whether an industry publication fits the Index. Only a 238px cover thumbnail exists on the publisher site.

11-arc-poetry-magazine.name: Arc Poetry Magazine
11-arc-poetry-magazine.description: Arc Poetry Magazine is Canada's poetry magazine, printing new poems, translations, reviews, interviews and close reading columns three times a year, with a featured artist on the cover and inside. Each issue also carries the results of one of its contests, such as the Poem of the Year. It is for poets, students and anyone following contemporary Canadian poetry.
11-arc-poetry-magazine.note: Frequency derived from cadence (three issues a year since 2025). Latest issue date is the shop listing date for Arc 110.

12-art-review.name: ArtReview
12-art-review.reason: Not independently published. ArtReview Ltd states on its own about page that it is part of Meta Media Group, the Hong Kong listed media group.

13-autre-magazine.name: Autre
13-autre-magazine.description: Autre is a large format Los Angeles magazine on art, fashion and culture, with each issue built around one theme such as surveillance or wellness. Issues run several hundred pages of long interviews, essays and photography, carry four alternative covers and include a digital edition with every print order. It is for readers of contemporary art and culture criticism who want a theme driven, collectable object twice a year.
13-autre-magazine.note: Publisher name from the site copyright line. Cover images carry a rendered drop shadow; a fully flat file was not found.

14-backstage-talks.name: Backstage Talks
14-backstage-talks.description: Backstage Talks is a magazine of long conversations with designers, studio founders and creative directors about the business behind the work, from pricing and growth to how decisions get made. The latest issue centres on complexity and change and adds a short crash course in complexity science. It suits working designers, studio owners and design students.
14-backstage-talks.note: Published by Büro Milk (Milk Studio s.r.o., Bratislava). Cadence is roughly one issue every one to two years, so frequency is irregular. Price EUR 25 and issue date from brot.sk, the shop the publisher's buy button points to.

01-blanc.name: Blanc
01-blanc.description: Blanc is a quarterly fashion, art and music magazine built around cover stories with musicians and artists, long interviews and fashion editorials, printed at 315 by 230 mm. It gives space to voices the mainstream glossies tend to pass over. It is for readers of culture and fashion magazines who want a broader cast than the newsstand offers.
01-blanc.note: Publisher site gives no city (US title). Imprint is Blanc Media, Inc.

06-c-41.name: C41
06-c-41.description: C41 is a biannual from a Milan production studio that brings photography, design, fashion and visual culture together around one theme per issue. Issues run to around 300 perfect bound pages with two alternative covers and long portfolio features. It is for readers of image led culture magazines and people working in photography and design.
06-c-41.note: Legal entity not spelled out on the site (registered office in Arcore, MB); recorded under the imprint name. Publisher cover image URLs reset connections from this session, so a stockist copy may be needed.

17-cv2.name: Contemporary Verse 2
17-cv2.description: Contemporary Verse 2, known as CV2, is a Winnipeg poetry quarterly founded in 1975 that prints new poems alongside interviews, essays and reviews of recent collections. Issues alternate between themed and open numbers and carry the results of the magazine's own contests. It is for readers and writers of contemporary poetry, especially Canadian work.
17-cv2.note: Published by Contemporary Verse 2 Inc., a registered charity. CSV name was CV2.

01-dna.name: DNA
01-dna.description: DNA is an Australian monthly for gay men that mixes news features, celebrity interviews and long reads on LGBTQIA+ life with extensive model and fashion photography. Every issue carries a cover interview, a themed feature and several photographic portfolios. It is for readers who want a glossy, international gay lifestyle title with an Australian base.
01-dna.note: Publisher describes itself as an independently owned LGBTQIA+ Australian media company, which is the basis for the queer-led tag. Shop prices in USD. Distributor hint only said DNA; no other print magazine of that name was found.

04-double-blind.name: DoubleBlind
04-double-blind.reason: Shop issue list ends at Issue 12 (November 2024); confirm whether any 2025 or 2026 print issue exists before adding.

06-dune.name: Dune
06-dune.reason: Historic Tokyo title published 1993 to 2008. The KD Presse listings behind the hint are 1990s back issues, so there is no print issue since January 2025 and no current publisher.

01-fucking-young.name: Fucking Young!
01-fucking-young.description: Fucking Young! is a Barcelona menswear and youth culture magazine that builds each issue around one theme, recently Dopamine, Dreamcore and Transparency. It runs long photographic fashion stories with young models and musicians plus interviews with designers across roughly 400 pages and several collectable covers. It is for readers who follow menswear, emerging photographers and pop culture.
01-fucking-young.note: About page lists the publisher as ABHFYA.com at a Barcelona address; recorded under the magazine's name. Best cover found is 682px.

02-full-pour.name: Full Pour
02-full-pour.description: Full Pour is a quarterly American magazine about drinks of every kind, with sections on wine, beer, spirits, cannabis infused drinks and zero proof, plus coffee and tea. Each hundred page issue mixes reported features on producers and farming with short interviews and skips scores and buying guides altogether. It is for curious drinkers and trade readers who want cross category reading rather than a single beverage title.
02-full-pour.note: Only a PO box in Brookfield, Connecticut is given as an address.

03-gayletter.name: GAYLETTER
03-gayletter.description: GAYLETTER is a New York queer culture magazine that grew out of a weekly events newsletter. Each issue pairs cover stories with artists and performers, shot by photographers such as Collier Schorr, with interviews, nightlife, art and fashion photography, usually in two cover editions. It is for readers interested in contemporary gay and queer culture and the New York scene.
03-gayletter.note: Queer-led tag rests on the publisher's own description of itself as a queer publication; please confirm. No street address published; New York from the publisher's own framing.

04-girls-like-us.name: Girls Like Us
04-girls-like-us.description: Girls Like Us is a Brussels queer feminist magazine devoted to women and trans people working in art, culture and activism, with each issue built around a theme such as economy, biography or the club scene. Issues combine essays, personal writing, conversations and artists' visual contributions, and the latest was made together with a closing lesbian and trans bar. It is for readers of feminist and queer theory, art writing and small press culture.
04-girls-like-us.note: Cadence is irregular. Issue 15 date from the Antenne listing (October 2026) with the cover reading Issue Fifteen 2026.

05-glory.name: Glory
05-glory.description: Glory is a football magazine that treats each issue as a travel document about one country, city or club away from the big leagues, with recent editions on San Marino, Hamburg, Hibernian and Mexico ahead of the 2026 World Cup. Issues run to around 240 pages of film photography from stadiums and streets, long essays, interviews and practical notes for visiting. It is for readers who love football for its fan culture and places, and for travel readers who use the game as a way in.
05-glory.note: Issue numbering is not shown in the publisher shop; No. 12 comes from the printed cover. Shop price GBP 12 while the printed cover says GBP 15.

06-handvaerk.name: HÅNDVÆRK bookazine
06-handvaerk.description: HÅNDVÆRK bookazine is a Danish publication about craft and making, printed in separate Danish and English editions twice a year and organised around one theme per issue. Each number is a sequence of long interviews and photographic portraits of makers, designers and small workshops, taking in ceramics, textiles, furniture, architecture and food. It is for readers interested in Scandinavian craft, materials and slow design.
06-handvaerk.note: Published by its designer and photographer under the bookazine's name; no company name found. City Frederiksberg is inferred. Price DKK 250.

07-herdes.name: HERDES
07-herdes.description: HERDES is a hardcover travel and fashion bookazine from Barcelona in which every issue is devoted to one destination, recently Türkiye, Andalusia and Cambodia. Each volume of more than 250 pages combines fashion editorials shot on location with essays on local culture and craft, a travel handbook section and features on hotels. It is for design minded travellers who want a collectable object rather than a guidebook.
07-herdes.note: Publisher legal name WELOVEPAPER, SL. Both cover candidates are described as product mockups; check the stored file.

09-hype-and-hyper.name: Hype&Hyper
09-hype-and-hyper.description: Hype&Hyper is a Budapest annual about Central and Eastern Europe, covering strategy, business, design and lifestyle from the region's own point of view. Each themed print issue mixes essays on geopolitics and regional economies with design, architecture, food and art features, in English and Hungarian. It is for readers interested in the culture and business of the region.
09-hype-and-hyper.note: No legal company name found. Price HUF 3950.

10-inque.name: Inque
10-inque.description: Inque is a large format annual literary and arts magazine printed without advertising and planned as a ten issue run. Each number is divided into non fiction, fiction, interviews and art and runs to around 220 pages of new writing from established novelists and essayists alongside commissioned artwork. It is for readers who collect literary print and want long reads in a heavyweight object.
10-inque.note: Inque has no website or shop by design, so publisher website, publisher price and subscribe URL are blank. Facts come from stockist listings and press.

11-its-freezing-in-la.name: It's Freezing in LA!
11-its-freezing-in-la.description: It's Freezing in LA! is a British magazine about the climate crisis that pairs essays and reportage with commissioned illustration, each issue built around a theme such as plants, knowledge or power. Issues run to about sixty pages and bring together writing on energy, politics, ecology and culture by emerging writers. It is for readers who want longer, idea led climate writing with a strong visual identity.
11-its-freezing-in-la.note: Non-profit company no. 11765188; London from the registered office.

01-little-white-lies.name: Little White Lies
01-little-white-lies.description: Little White Lies builds each print issue around one new film, with a commissioned illustrated cover and a long run of interviews and essays on that release before turning to reviews and features on the rest of cinema. The illustration heavy design has been its signature since 2005. It is for readers who follow arthouse and mainstream cinema and want criticism with a strong visual identity.
01-little-white-lies.note: In Neesh's TCO pilot. Price GBP 10 from magCulture because the publisher's shop blocks automated requests.

02-log.name: Log
02-log.description: Log is a text led journal of architectural criticism and commentary from New York that covers buildings, cities, technology and design culture through essays, interviews and short observations rather than image spreads. Issues are mostly open themed with occasional thematic numbers, three times a year. It is for architects, students and scholars who follow architectural thinking closely.
02-log.note: Issue date is the store listing date for Log 67.

03-lost.name: LOST
03-lost.description: LOST is a bilingual English and Chinese travel annual built around first person stories of self discovery rather than destination guides, with around ten long personal narratives per issue and commissioned photography. It is printed as a thick volume on uncoated paper. It suits readers who like slow, reflective travel writing and Chinese language perspectives on travel.
03-lost.note: Neither the magazine site nor the publisher site states a country. Singapore is inferred from SGD pricing and press coverage; please confirm.

04-lovewant.name: LoveWant
04-lovewant.description: LoveWant is a large format Sydney fashion, photography and art magazine with multiple collectable covers per issue, built from portraits, fashion stories shot by its own editors and interviews with musicians and artists. Text is sparse and the 240 pages read as a printed moodboard. It is for fashion image collectors and people who follow photographers and models rather than trends.
04-lovewant.note: No publisher shop; issues are sold through Perimeter, so no publisher cover price. Publisher calls it bi-monthly but the cadence is about four issues a year.

05-maisonneuve.name: Maisonneuve
05-maisonneuve.description: Maisonneuve is a Montreal general interest quarterly that mixes reported features on social and political questions with essays, fiction, poetry and comics, plus review sections on books, music and film and some work translated from Quebec French. Each issue carries a cover story on a current Canadian subject. It suits readers who want long form Canadian journalism and literary writing in one magazine.
05-maisonneuve.note: Single issue price could not be read (subscription page is client rendered). Best cover found is 600px.

06-milk.name: MilK
06-milk.description: MilK is a French language quarterly about family life with children, covering children's fashion, interiors and home tours, design objects, travel and parenting. Photographic fashion stories sit alongside features on makers and artists, and covers usually show a family or child in a styled home. It is for style conscious parents.
06-milk.note: Publisher shop is fully client rendered, so no cover price. Publisher image URL returned 403 to this session.

08-mulieris.name: Mulieris Magazine
08-mulieris.description: Mulieris Magazine is an English language art and culture annual from Italy that publishes photography, visual art, essays and interviews by and about women, with each issue built around one theme such as home and migration. It draws on a large international pool of contributors. It is for readers interested in contemporary women's art practice and themed visual anthologies.
08-mulieris.note: Publisher site says only based in Italy; no city found, which the import requires for a non-US title. The identity tag women-led was not applied because the site does not state it as such.

09-musicworks.name: Musicworks
09-musicworks.description: Musicworks is a Toronto magazine about experimental music and sound art, with long profiles of composers, improvisers and electronic artists, festival and album reviews, and a companion CD of recordings tied to each issue. It appears three times a year. It is for musicians, composers and listeners who follow new and exploratory music.
09-musicworks.note: Price CAD 20.95 is the magazine with CD; the magazine alone is CAD 10.95. Issue 155 is on pre-order with a placeholder image, so Issue 154 is recorded.

01-p-l-s-magazine.name: PLS
01-p-l-s-magazine.description: PLS is the French language magazine of the Palais de Tokyo, issued with each new exhibition season. Every number takes one theme, such as territory or the body, and gathers essays and visual contributions from the artists and researchers connected to the current shows. It is for readers following French contemporary art and the Palais de Tokyo programme.
01-p-l-s-magazine.note: Published by a public art centre rather than a company; independence is a judgement call for review. Price EUR 5 is from KD Presse. Best cover found is 606px.

02-permanent-style.name: Permanent Style
02-permanent-style.description: Permanent Style is a print menswear magazine grown out of the website of the same name, focused on tailoring, craft and the makers behind classic men's clothing. Each issue carries long interviews and reportage, often built around a city or region, with recent numbers on Scotland and Los Angeles. It is for readers interested in bespoke clothing, shoemaking and well made menswear.
02-permanent-style.note: The publisher's main site blocks automated requests, so London is taken from general knowledge of the title rather than its own pages.

03-port.name: Port
03-port.description: Port is a large format London biannual covering culture and style through long interviews with actors, writers, designers and architects, photo led fashion stories and essays on art, design, food and literature. Issues run to around 300 pages with several covers. It is for readers who want a glossy but text heavy general culture magazine with a menswear slant.
03-port.note: Issue 39 is on pre-order; Issue 38 is recorded. Exact release date of Issue 38 estimated as June 2026.

04-prairie-fire.name: Prairie Fire
04-prairie-fire.description: Prairie Fire is a Winnipeg literary quarterly publishing new fiction, poetry and creative non fiction, with themed issues and annual writing contests. It is printed as a perfect bound journal and draws on writers from the Prairies and across Canada. It is for readers of literary journals and emerging Canadian writing.
04-prairie-fire.note: The publisher site sits behind a bot wall; facts come from cached pages and the shop. Fall 2026 issue recorded at September 2026.

05-profane.name: Profane
05-profane.description: Profane is a French biannual art review devoted to amateurs, self taught makers and collectors working outside the official art world. Each issue mixes portraits, interviews and photo stories of people who make or collect for love rather than career, set in experimental graphic design. It is for readers of art, craft and outsider culture, in French.
05-profane.note: Paris from stockist listings; the publisher site gives no postal address.

06-pulp-literature.name: Pulp Literature
06-pulp-literature.description: Pulp Literature is a Canadian quarterly digest of genre fiction, poetry and comics, leaning towards science fiction, fantasy and mystery alongside literary work. Issues run serialised novellas, contest winners and feature authors in a pocketable, inexpensive format. It is for readers who like story driven fiction they can carry around.
06-pulp-literature.note: City (Langley, BC) from the Magazines BC member listing rather than the publisher's own pages.

07-ralph.name: Ralph
07-ralph.description: Ralph is a glossy London quarterly about pop culture and entertainment, with long interviews with comedians, musicians, television people and animators alongside photo stories and humour pieces. It is deliberately playful and broad rather than niche. It is for readers who want a fun, mainstream leaning entertainment magazine in print.
07-ralph.note: Published by a creative agency as its own editorial product rather than a client magazine. Trim size and page count from magCulture.

09-record-culture.name: Record Culture Magazine
09-record-culture.reason: Same title as Record Magazine already on the Index: record-magazine.com is Record Culture Magazine's own site (publisher Record Creative Limited, Cork, founded in New York in 2016).

01-subterrain-magazine.name: subTerrain
01-subterrain-magazine.description: subTerrain is a Vancouver literary magazine mixing short fiction, poetry, essays and commentary with book reviews and columns on chapbooks and small press publishing. Each issue carries a featured visual artist on the cover and inside, and some numbers are built around a theme such as dreams or trash. It is for readers of contemporary Canadian and international writing with a stake in the small press scene.
01-subterrain-magazine.note: Issue 103 is labelled Spring 2026 and recorded at March 2026. Best cover found is 468px.

02-synth-history.name: Synth History
02-synth-history.description: Synth History is a thick, small format print zine about synthesizers and the people who use them, built from long interviews with electronic and pop musicians, producers and instrument designers about their gear, process and influences. Recurring sections ask artists for their favourite records or three quick questions. It is for synth players, producers and electronic music fans who like gear talk in a collectable annual edition.
02-synth-history.note: The publisher's Wix shop renders client side, so price and stock could not be read; Issue 6 (2026) is on pre-order and Issue 5 (2025) is recorded. Cover from a stockist.

03-temple-magazine.name: Temple Magazine
03-temple-magazine.description: Temple Magazine is a large format annual from Paris that gathers interviews, portfolios and essays on contemporary art, fashion, design and new media around a theme such as botanics or Japan. Each edition mixes art school graduates and emerging designers with established artists and often ships with several covers and heavily art directed typography. It is for readers who follow fashion school and gallery culture in France and Switzerland.
03-temple-magazine.note: Paris from the studio's contact page and launch events; no postal address on the magazine site.

04-the-aficionados.name: The Aficionados
04-the-aficionados.description: The Aficionados is a series of travel and design magazines in which each edition is devoted to a region or a kind of hotel, from family run places around the Mediterranean to Alpine properties. Each 148 page edition profiles the architecture, interiors and owners of the hotels, grouped by design register, with makers and products alongside. It is for travellers, hoteliers and interiors readers who use it as a sourcebook for characterful places to stay.
04-the-aficionados.note: The publisher also runs a hotel directory and places copies in featured hotels' rooms; please decide whether that makes it a customer publication. Frequency inferred from a winter and summer rhythm.

05-the-capilano-review.name: The Capilano Review
05-the-capilano-review.publisher_name: The Capilano Review Contemporary Arts Society
05-the-capilano-review.description: The Capilano Review is a Vancouver journal of experimental writing and contemporary art, running since 1972, that pairs poetry, fiction and essays with full colour artist projects, interviews and reviews. Issues are often themed or guest edited, recently on speculative feminisms and on prison abolition, and draw on West Coast and Indigenous writers alongside international contributors. It is for readers of avant garde Canadian literature and visual art.
05-the-capilano-review.note: Issue 4.7 page still said pre-order while marked in stock and called the current issue.

06-the-dorchester-review.name: The Dorchester Review
06-the-dorchester-review.description: The Dorchester Review is a Canadian journal of historical commentary and book reviews, with long essays on Canadian and British history, biography, politics and culture written from a conservative standpoint. Each quarterly edition runs reviews and features by academics, former political staff and journalists. It is for readers interested in Canadian history and conservative political argument in print.
06-the-dorchester-review.note: Volume and number not shown; Summer 2026 read from the cover file. Recorded at June 2026.

07-the-grand-tourist.name: The Grand Tourist
07-the-grand-tourist.description: The Grand Tourist is a hardcover, linen bound magazine that grew out of a design and luxury interview podcast, with around 400 pages per volume of long interviews, commissioned photography and travel dispatches on interiors, architecture, fashion, jewellery, art, food and hotels. Each issue appears in several cover editions. It is for readers and design professionals who follow the high end of interiors, craft and travel and want a book like object.
07-the-grand-tourist.note: Publisher legal name Design Media LLC; US city not stated. Several cover editions are tied to featured brands.

08-the-greatest.name: The Greatest
08-the-greatest.description: The Greatest is a large format men's fashion magazine published twice a year from Milan, each issue built around one theme and issued with several collectable covers. Inside are long fashion editorials by an international roster of photographers and interviews with actors, designers, artists and athletes, running well past 400 pages. It is for readers who collect menswear and fashion photography titles.
08-the-greatest.note: No legal company name on the site; recorded under the imprint name.

02-turps-magazine.name: Turps
02-turps-magazine.description: Turps is a magazine about painting in which the writers are painters rather than critics. Each issue carries interviews, studio conversations and essays on contemporary and historical painters, with no advertising. It is for practising painters, art students and readers who want painters' own views on painting.
02-turps-magazine.note: Single issue price not shown on the publisher site. Cadence is uneven (Nov 2024, Jul 2025, with Issue 31 announced), so frequency is irregular.

03-typeone.name: TYPEONE Magazine
03-typeone.description: TYPEONE Magazine is an English language print magazine about typography and graphic design, with studio interviews, opinion pieces, industry insight and career advice. Each issue is themed and guest designed, and alternate limited edition covers are common. It is for graphic designers, type designers and students.
03-typeone.note: typeonemagazine.com now redirects elsewhere; the live site is type-01.com. Issue 11 is on pre-order, so Issue 10 is recorded.

04-umbigo.name: Umbigo
04-umbigo.description: Umbigo is a Portuguese contemporary art magazine, published since 2002, that builds each issue around a theme with essays, artist profiles, commissioned art projects and an exhibition section. Since issue 68 it has appeared in separate Portuguese and English editions with two alternative artist covers. It is for readers following contemporary art in Portugal and the Lusophone world.
04-umbigo.note: Issue date from the cover file upload timestamp (October 2026).

05-unemployed.name: Unemployed
05-unemployed.description: Unemployed is a large format, image led New York magazine built around commissioned fashion and art photography, with each issue redesigned around a theme. Issues appear roughly once a year in small runs and carry contributors from fashion photography and contemporary art. It is for collectors of photography and fashion publications.
05-unemployed.note: Cover images are photographs of the physical issue rather than flat artwork.

06-union-magazine.name: Union
06-union-magazine.description: Union is a Tokyo made, English language fashion and photography magazine produced as a cloth bound hardcover of around 184 pages. Each issue gathers long photo stories by international photographers with very little text, built to still look right decades from now. It is for readers of fashion photography and collectors of photo books.
06-union-magazine.note: Publisher says twice yearly but the cadence is slower (Issue 18 in 2023, Issue 19 in November 2025), so frequency is irregular.

07-vanish.name: Vanish
07-vanish.description: Vanish is a print magazine about the overlap of outdoor life and urban style, covering technical apparel, design, architecture, travel and the people shaping outdoor culture. Issues are themed paperbacks of around 200 pages with brand profiles, interviews and fashion style photography. It is for readers interested in gorpcore fashion, outdoor design and adventure travel.
07-vanish.note: No publisher shop, so no publisher price (printed cover carries GBP 20, EUR 24, USD 28). Issue 3 date from a retailer listing.

09-viper.name: Viper
09-viper.reason: No print issue since January 2025. The publisher's own site still presents Winter 2024 as the latest print issue.

12-we-jazz.name: We Jazz Magazine
12-we-jazz.description: We Jazz Magazine is a quarterly English language journal about jazz and creative music from Helsinki, each issue built around a focus artist alongside long profiles, a record collecting column, album and live reviews and photo essays. The 128 page print edition is sold with a bonus digital album. It is for listeners of jazz, improvised and experimental music.
